title: Lock the lid and idle the Radeon on 15-inch 2016–2017 MacBook Pros
author: shawnyeager
body:
## Summary

On the 15-inch 2016–2017 Radeon MacBooks, closing the lid no longer suspends. That path does not resume, so the machine stays on, locks, idles the GPU, and **disables the internal output** so the 560 stops scanning out.

Independent of the Touch Bar and CS8409 speaker work. Verified on MacBookPro14,3. 13-inch T1 models are Intel-only and are not included.

## Why

Stock lid-suspend is a hard reboot on these boards.

Stay-on with the lid closed still cooked the chassis. amdgpu sat on `3D_FULL_SCREEN` (~13 W at 0% busy). Backlight 0 still scanned out eDP. Hyprland DPMS did too — the CRTC stayed up. Stock `key_press_enables_dpms` / `mouse_move_enables_dpms` then turned scanout back on. Clamshell then force-enabled the internal panel on every `monitorremoved`, which undid the blank.

A `powerprofilesctl set power-saver` overlay on lid close put BCM43602 (`14e4:43ba`) into PCI D3/ASPM. `brcmfmac` does not come back from that.

## What

- Detector is `MacBookPro13,3` / `14,3` only.
- Lid switch locks. systemd refuses suspend and hibernate. The menu hides those rows.
- The discrete GPU stays bound. `POWER_SAVING` lets Polaris drop clocks at idle. This is not a GPU power-off.
- Lid close disables the internal output (`hl.monitor({ disabled = true })`) and persists that in a Hyprland toggle so a reload does not bring the panel back. Key/mouse DPMS-wake is held off. It does **not** set power-saver.
- Clamshell does not force-enable the internal panel while the lid is shut with no external, so a `monitorremoved` event cannot undo the disable.
- Open drops the toggle, restores the panel, brightness, the wake flags, and `omarchy-powerprofiles-set autodetect`.
- BCM43602 stays PCI-awake: udev `power/control=on` and `d3cold_allowed=0`, applied at install and by migration `1788634178`.
- A docked lid close skips the overlay so the external display stays usable.
- Migration seeds AC=`balanced` only if the user has never chosen a profile.
- The NVMe d3cold unit follows `nvme0` instead of `0000:01:00.0` (the Radeon on these machines).

No mux, no rEFInd, no voicing.

Related: #7064, #7140

## Test plan

- [x] `test/shell.d/mbp15-dgpu-test.sh` (detector, idle profile, lid overlay, output disable, wake-flag save/restore, wifi PCI pin, no lid-close power-saver)
- [x] `test/shell.d/lid-close-test.sh` (lock, then clamshell, then 15-inch chill)
- [x] `test/shell.d/monitor-clamshell-scale-test.sh` (clamshell does not re-enable a shut undocked panel)
- [x] MacBookPro14,3: POWER_SAVING idles ~214–320 MHz; lid lock + backlight 0; open restores
- [ ] Live lid close after this commit: confirm eDP is disabled (`hyprctl monitors all`) and GPU power drops, and that a key/mouse does not bring the panel back. Tests cover the helper; that close was not run in this session.
- [ ] MacBookPro14,3: lid close leaves `wlan` up; `power/control` on `14e4:43ba` stays `on`.

@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+# omarchy:summary=Let the 15-inch Radeon idle without nailing 3D clocks
+# omarchy:hidden=true
+
+# Hyprland keeps amdgpu on 3D_FULL_SCREEN under `auto`. That profile's
+# down-hysteresis holds Polaris on the top sclk rung at 0% busy. Switch
+# to manual + POWER_SAVING so clocks drop when idle and can still climb.
+# Not a GPU power-off.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+here=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
+"$here/omarchy-hw-apple-mbp15-dgpu" || exit 0
+
+amdgpu_dev() {
+  if [[ -n ${OMARCHY_MBP15_AMDGPU_DEV:-} ]]; then
+    printf '%s\n' "$OMARCHY_MBP15_AMDGPU_DEV"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  local d
+  for d in /sys/bus/pci/devices/*; do
+    [[ -r $d/vendor && $(cat "$d/vendor") == 0x1002 ]] || continue
+    [[ -e $d/power_dpm_force_performance_level ]] || continue
+    printf '%s\n' "$d"
+    return 0
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+dev=$(amdgpu_dev) || exit 0
+
+for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
+  [[ -w $dev/power_dpm_force_performance_level ]] && break
+  sleep 0.1
+done
+[[ -w $dev/power_dpm_force_performance_level ]] || exit 0
+
+echo manual >"$dev/power_dpm_force_performance_level"
+
+profile=2
+if [[ -r $dev/pp_power_profile_mode ]]; then
+  profile=$(awk '/POWER_SAVING/ { print $1; exit }' "$dev/pp_power_profile_mode")
+  : "${profile:=2}"
+fi
+echo "$profile" >"$dev/pp_power_profile_mode"
+
+if [[ -w $dev/pp_dpm_sclk ]]; then
+  rungs=$(awk -F: '/^[0-9]/ { printf "%s ", $1 }' "$dev/pp_dpm_sclk")
+  [[ -n $rungs ]] && printf '%s\n' "$rungs" >"$dev/pp_dpm_sclk"
+fi
+if [[ -w $dev/pp_dpm_mclk ]]; then
+  rungs=$(awk -F: '/^[0-9]/ { printf "%s ", $1 }' "$dev/pp_dpm_mclk")
+  [[ -n $rungs ]] && printf '%s\n' "$rungs" >"$dev/pp_dpm_mclk"
+fi

@@ -0,0 +1,163 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+# omarchy:summary=Stop driving the panel while a 15-inch Radeon lid is shut
+# omarchy:hidden=true
+# omarchy:args=<close|open>
+
+# Temporary overlay only. Does not write Omarchy's remembered AC/battery
+# profile. Close: save brightness, hold DPMS-wake keys/mouse off, disable
+# the internal output. DPMS and backlight-off still leave the 560 scanning
+# out eDP; disabling the output tears the CRTC down. Do not set
+# power-saver: that puts BCM43602 into PCI D3 and brcmfmac does not come
+# back. Open: drop the disable flag, restore the panel, brightness and
+# wake flags, autodetect (unsticks a profile a previous close already set).
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+cmd=${1:-}
+case $cmd in
+  close | open) ;;
+  *)
+    echo "Usage: omarchy-hw-apple-mbp15-lid close|open" >&2
+    exit 2
+    ;;
+esac
+
+here=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
+"$here/omarchy-hw-apple-mbp15-dgpu" || exit 0
+
+state_dir=${OMARCHY_MBP15_LID_STATE:-${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/omarchy/mbp15-lid}
+toggle_dir=${OMARCHY_MBP15_TOGGLE_DIR:-${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/omarchy/toggles/hypr}
+toggle_file=$toggle_dir/internal-monitor-lid-closed.lua
+mkdir -p "$state_dir" "$toggle_dir"
+
+backlight_get() {
+  if [[ -n ${OMARCHY_MBP15_BRIGHTNESS_GET:-} ]]; then
+    "$OMARCHY_MBP15_BRIGHTNESS_GET"
+    return
+  fi
+  command -v brightnessctl >/dev/null || return 1
+  brightnessctl -d gmux_backlight get
+}
+
+backlight_set() {
+  if [[ -n ${OMARCHY_MBP15_BRIGHTNESS_SET:-} ]]; then
+    "$OMARCHY_MBP15_BRIGHTNESS_SET" "$1"
+    return
+  fi
+  command -v brightnessctl >/dev/null || return 0
+  brightnessctl -d gmux_backlight set "$1" >/dev/null
+}
+
+laptop_output() {
+  local internal
+  internal=$(omarchy-hyprland-monitor-laptop 2>/dev/null || true)
+  [[ -n $internal && $internal =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || return 1
+  printf '%s\n' "$internal"
+}
+
+# Disable the laptop panel so the 560 stops scanning out. Clamshell already
+# returned above; this only runs when the internal display is the one in use.
+# The toggle file keeps it off across Hyprland reloads; eval applies now.
+panel_disable() {
+  local internal
+  if [[ -n ${OMARCHY_MBP15_MONITOR:-} ]]; then
+    "$OMARCHY_MBP15_MONITOR" disable
+    printf 'hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", disabled = true })\n' >"$toggle_file"
+    return
+  fi
+  internal=$(laptop_output) || return 0
+  printf 'hl.monitor({ output = "%s", disabled = true })\n' "$internal" >"$toggle_file"
+  hyprctl eval "hl.monitor({ output = \"$internal\", disabled = true })" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+}
+
+panel_enable() {
+  local internal
+  rm -f "$toggle_file"
+  if [[ -n ${OMARCHY_MBP15_MONITOR:-} ]]; then
+    "$OMARCHY_MBP15_MONITOR" enable
+    return
+  fi
+  internal=$(laptop_output) || return 0
+  hyprctl eval "hl.monitor({ output = \"$internal\", mode = \"preferred\" })" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+}
+
+# Stock misc.key_press_enables_dpms / mouse_move_enables_dpms are true, so any
+# key or mouse motion re-enables DPMS after we turn the panel off.
+dpms_wake_get() {
+  if [[ -n ${OMARCHY_MBP15_DPMS_WAKE:-} ]]; then
+    "$OMARCHY_MBP15_DPMS_WAKE" get
+    return
+  fi
+  local key mouse
+  key=$(hyprctl -j getoption misc.key_press_enables_dpms 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.bool' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
+  mouse=$(hyprctl -j getoption misc.mouse_move_enables_dpms 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.bool' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
+  [[ $key == true || $key == false ]] || return 1
+  [[ $mouse == true || $mouse == false ]] || return 1
+  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$key" "$mouse"
+}
+
+dpms_wake_set() {
+  local key=$1 mouse=$2
+  if [[ -n ${OMARCHY_MBP15_DPMS_WAKE:-} ]]; then
+    "$OMARCHY_MBP15_DPMS_WAKE" set "$key" "$mouse"
+    return
+  fi
+  hyprctl eval "hl.config({ misc = { key_press_enables_dpms = $key, mouse_move_enables_dpms = $mouse } })" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+}
+
+dpms_wake_save() {
+  local previous
+  [[ -f $state_dir/dpms-wake ]] && return 0
+  previous=$(dpms_wake_get) || return 0
+  [[ $previous == $'true\ttrue' || $previous == $'true\tfalse' || $previous == $'false\ttrue' || $previous == $'false\tfalse' ]] || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$previous" >"$state_dir/dpms-wake"
+}
+
+dpms_wake_save_and_disable() {
+  dpms_wake_save
+  [[ -f $state_dir/dpms-wake ]] || return 0
+  dpms_wake_set false false
+}
+
+dpms_wake_restore() {
+  local key mouse
+  [[ -r $state_dir/dpms-wake ]] || return 0
+  IFS=$'\t' read -r key mouse <"$state_dir/dpms-wake" || true
+  if [[ $key != true && $key != false ]] || [[ $mouse != true && $mouse != false ]]; then
+    rm -f "$state_dir/dpms-wake"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  dpms_wake_set "$key" "$mouse"
+  rm -f "$state_dir/dpms-wake"
+}
+
+if [[ $cmd == close ]]; then
+  if command -v omarchy-hw-external-monitors >/dev/null && omarchy-hw-external-monitors; then
+    exit 0
+  fi
+  if command -v omarchy-hw-laptop-closed >/dev/null && ! omarchy-hw-laptop-closed; then
+    exit 0
+  fi
+
+  current=$(backlight_get 2>/dev/null || true)
+  if [[ -n ${current:-} && $current != 0 ]]; then
+    printf '%s\n' "$current" >"$state_dir/backlight"
+  fi
+  # Hold wake-from-DPMS off before blanking, or a key/mouse re-enables scanout.
+  dpms_wake_save_and_disable
+  panel_disable
+  backlight_set 0 || true
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+if command -v omarchy-hw-laptop-closed >/dev/null && omarchy-hw-laptop-closed; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+panel_enable
+if [[ -r $state_dir/backlight ]]; then
+  backlight_set "$(cat "$state_dir/backlight")" || true
+fi
+dpms_wake_restore
+omarchy-powerprofiles-set autodetect >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

@@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+# omarchy:summary=Keep the 15-inch Broadcom Wi-Fi card out of PCI D3
+# omarchy:hidden=true
+
+# power-saver and PCI ASPM put BCM43602 into a state brcmfmac does not
+# recover from. Force runtime PM off. Not a driver reload.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+here=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
+"$here/omarchy-hw-apple-mbp15-dgpu" || exit 0
+
+wifi_devs() {
+  if [[ -n ${OMARCHY_MBP15_WIFI_DEV:-} ]]; then
+    printf '%s\n' "$OMARCHY_MBP15_WIFI_DEV"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  local d
+  for d in /sys/bus/pci/devices/*; do
+    [[ -r $d/vendor && $(cat "$d/vendor") == 0x14e4 ]] || continue
+    [[ -r $d/device && $(cat "$d/device") == 0x43ba ]] || continue
+    printf '%s\n' "$d"
+  done
+}
+
+while IFS= read -r dev; do
+  [[ -n $dev ]] || continue
+  if [[ -w $dev/power/control ]]; then
+    echo on >"$dev/power/control"
+  fi
+  if [[ -w $dev/d3cold_allowed ]]; then
+    echo 0 >"$dev/d3cold_allowed"
+  fi
+done < <(wifi_devs)

+if omarchy-hw-laptop-closed && ! omarchy-hw-external-monitors; then
+  omarchy-hw-apple-mbp15-lid close >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+fi

+# 15" 2016–2017 Radeon: apply POWER_SAVING when amdgpu binds.
+# The helper no-ops on other hardware.
+ACTION=="bind", SUBSYSTEM=="pci", DRIVER=="amdgpu", RUN+="/usr/bin/omarchy-hw-apple-mbp15-amdgpu-idle"

@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
+# 15" 2016–2017: BCM43602 (14e4:43ba) dies if PCI runtime PM or D3cold
+# takes the card. Same stay-awake as the Thunderbolt xHCI quirk.
+# The helper no-ops on other hardware; this rule matches the chip.
+ACTION=="add", SUBSYSTEM=="pci", ATTR{vendor}=="0x14e4", ATTR{device}=="0x43ba", ATTR{power/control}="on", ATTR{d3cold_allowed}="0"

+# 15" 2016–2017 MacBook Pros with a Radeon cannot resume from S3 or s2idle.
+# Lock the lid, refuse sleep, and put the discrete GPU on POWER_SAVING so a

+# stays bound.

+  echo "Detected 15-inch MacBook Pro with Radeon; sleep does not resume"
+
+  # shellcheck source=mbp15-dgpu.sh
+  source "$OMARCHY_INSTALL/hardware/apple/mbp15-dgpu.sh"
+  mbp15_apply
+fi

@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+# Shared 15" Radeon MacBook helpers. Sourced; no shebang, no work on source.
+# S3/s2idle do not resume. Lid locks. Polaris stays bound and POWER_SAVING.
+# BCM43602 stays PCI-awake so a closed lid cannot D3 the radio.
+
+mbp15_logind_dest() {
+  printf '%s\n' "${OMARCHY_MBP15_LOGIND:-/etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/10-omarchy-apple-mbp15.conf}"
+}
+
+mbp15_sleep_dest() {
+  printf '%s\n' "${OMARCHY_MBP15_SLEEP:-/etc/systemd/sleep.conf.d/10-omarchy-apple-mbp15.conf}"
+}
+
+mbp15_udev_src() {
+  printf '%s\n' "${OMARCHY_MBP15_UDEV_SRC:-$OMARCHY_PATH/default/udev/apple-mbp15-amdgpu-idle.rules}"
+}
+
+mbp15_udev_dest() {
+  printf '%s\n' "${OMARCHY_MBP15_UDEV_DEST:-/etc/udev/rules.d/90-omarchy-apple-mbp15-amdgpu-idle.rules}"
+}
+
+mbp15_wifi_udev_src() {
+  printf '%s\n' "${OMARCHY_MBP15_WIFI_UDEV_SRC:-$OMARCHY_PATH/default/udev/apple-mbp15-wifi-pm.rules}"
+}
+
+mbp15_wifi_udev_dest() {
+  printf '%s\n' "${OMARCHY_MBP15_WIFI_UDEV_DEST:-/etc/udev/rules.d/90-omarchy-apple-mbp15-wifi-pm.rules}"
+}
+
+mbp15_write_sleep_policy() {
+  local dest
+  dest=$(mbp15_logind_dest)
+  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
+  cat >"$dest" <<'EOF'
+# 15" 2016–2017 MacBook Pro (Radeon): S3 and s2idle never resume.
+[Login]
+HandleLidSwitch=lock
+HandleLidSwitchExternalPower=lock
+HandleLidSwitchDocked=ignore
+EOF
+
+  dest=$(mbp15_sleep_dest)
+  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
+  cat >"$dest" <<'EOF'
+# 15" 2016–2017 MacBook Pro (Radeon): do not offer S3/S4.
+[Sleep]
+AllowSuspend=no
+AllowSuspendThenHibernate=no
+AllowHybridSleep=no
+AllowHibernation=no
+EOF
+}
+
+mbp15_write_amdgpu_idle() {
+  local dest
+  dest=$(mbp15_udev_dest)
+  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
+  cp -f "$(mbp15_udev_src)" "$dest"
+}
+
+mbp15_write_wifi_pm() {
+  local dest
+  dest=$(mbp15_wifi_udev_dest)
+  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"

comments.body:
I have lid-close suspend and resume working on a MacBookPro14,3, so I wanted to put numbers against the premise before this lands. The GPU-idling and clamshell half of this PR stands on its own either way — this is only about "stock lid-suspend is a hard reboot on these boards".

**Six suspend/resume cycles on a MacBookPro14,3**, stock `systemd-logind` lid path, Omarchy 4.0.3, kernel 7.2.3-arch1-3, Radeon Pro 560 + HD 630 over gmux, internal panel on the dGPU (`card1-eDP-1`; i915 has no connected output):

```
slept  0.7 min  ->  resumed in 0.67 s
slept  1.5 min  ->  resumed in 0.68 s
slept  2.0 min  ->  resumed in 0.69 s
slept 12.0 min  ->  resumed in 0.75 s
slept 10.2 min  ->  resumed in 0.76 s
slept  3.0 min  ->  resumed in 0.77 s
```

**One important qualification: the lid does not wake this machine — a keypress does.** Opening the lid leaves it asleep indefinitely (I left it 12 minutes and 10 minutes on two occasions); pressing any key resumes it in well under a second. The lid registers ACPI events but never a wake event — `/sys/kernel/debug/wakeup_sources` shows `PNP0C0D:00` with `event_count=2, wakeup_count=0`. `LID0` is already `*enabled` in `/proc/acpi/wakeup`, enabling `EC` as well changed nothing, and `acpi.ec_no_wakeup` is `N`. This matches discussion #4695, which notes lid-triggered wake is inconsistent across these hardware variants. So: suspend is reachable and resume is fast, but wake is keyboard-driven here.

**What it took, and why I think you are one step away from it.** You already pin the Wi-Fi awake — `power/control=on` and `d3cold_allowed=0` on `14e4:43ba`. That is exactly the treatment that turned out to be load-bearing; the difference is scope. Three things together:

1. `mem_sleep=s2idle`. `deep` never resumes on this board in any configuration I tried — the journal simply ends at `PM: suspend entry (deep)`.
2. `d3cold_allowed=0` on **every** PCI device, not only the BCM43602. Staged `/sys/power/pm_test` runs put the first blocker on the Wi-Fi exactly where you found it, but once that was pinned the same failure moved to the Thunderbolt bridges and the xHCI controllers behind them.
3. `power/control=on` on the `pcieport` bridges. They runtime-suspend into D3cold on their own when nothing is plugged in, and `d3cold_allowed` does not prevent it — by the time the flag is written they are already gone.

**2 and 3 are both required.** I dropped 3, kept 2, rebooted and closed the lid: no resume, journal ends at `PM: suspend entry (s2idle)` with zero D3cold errors logged before it. That was the only failed cycle of the seven.

**Two things that cost me hours, in case they save you some.**

`/sys/power/pm_test` is excellent for finding *which device* blocks the transition — it stages the suspend and auto-resumes after five seconds, so the journal survives, which a genuinely failed resume never does. It is **not** valid for comparing configurations: a device left stuck in D3cold by one trial stays stuck and contaminates the next. My staged runs said measure 2 alone was sufficient; the real lid close said otherwise, and the real lid close was right.

Do not unload `thunderbolt` around sleep. It unloads cleanly, but the controllers never re-probe — `timeout resetting host router`, `cannot enable interrupts`, `probe failed with error -22` — and Thunderbolt is dead until reboot. The `tb_cfg_read: -108` warnings on resume are noisy (about 14 per wake, ~1800 journal lines) but harmless; resume is 0.7 s with them present.

**Caveats.** One machine, one session. `s2idle` is not S3: the fans keep spinning with the lid shut, so your thermal argument for idling Polaris may well still apply *during* suspend — I have not measured chassis temperature over a long sleep, and that seems worth checking before treating these as alternatives. The T1 Touch Bar also goes dark across resume and needs its stack reloaded from a `system-sleep` hook, but that is #10825 territory rather than this PR's.

None of this touches the docked/clamshell half of your work. But if suspend is reachable on these boards, then `systemd` refusing suspend and hibernate outright, and hiding those menu rows, is a heavy hammer — and I wanted the measurements on the record before it lands.
